<p class="entry-meta">Published: <time class="entry-time">Dec 10, 2022</time> · by <span class="entry-author"><a href="https://khinskitchen.com/about-me/" class="entry-author-link" rel="author"><span class="entry-author-name">Khin</span></a></span> · This post may contain affiliate links.							</p></header><div class="entry-content"><div class="wprm-recipe wprm-recipe-snippet wprm-recipe-template-jump-to-without-button"><a href="#recipe" data-recipe="12653" style="color: #333333;" class="wprm-recipe-jump wprm-recipe-link wprm-jump-to-recipe-shortcode wprm-block-text-normal">Jump to Recipe</a>
</div>
<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Easy homemade Japanese prawn gyoza recipe made with succulent prawn, cabbage, and chive fillings. Pan-fried to crispy golden perfection and is so delicious! Perfect as an appetizer or savoury snack that all kids and adults can enjoy!</p>

<figure class="aligncenter size-full is-resized"><img decoding="async" fetchpriority="high" data-pin-url="https://khinskitchen.com/prawn-gyoza/?tp_image_id=12644" data-pin-title="Prawn Gyoza ( Pan-Fried Dumplings )" src="https://khinskitchen.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/12/prawn-gyoza-06.jpg" alt="A grey plate containing pan-fried Japanese prawn gyoza dumplings with chives and dipping sauce. <p class="wp-block-paragraph">We love to serve it with a quick homemade gyoza dipping sauce with a kick of chilli oil but feel free to serve it with soy sauce, sweet chilli sauce, or a choice of dipping sauce. </p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">Gyoza is a Japanese version of pan-fried dumplings and is popular across the world. It is also known as Japanese potstickers. Originated in China and is called ' jiaozi ' in Chinese and the ingredients and cooking methods are very similar in general. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph">We also love to cook dumplings with chicken and<a href="https://khinskitchen.com/pan-fried-dumplings-gyoza/"> Pan Fry Chicken Gyoza</a> and <a href="https://khinskitchen.com/crispy-deep-fried-dumplings/">Crispy Deep Fried Dumplings</a> are our family's favorite recipes that everyone loves! </p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Gyoza wrappers</strong> - is made of wheat flour, salt, and water. It is thinner and smaller than Chinese dumpling wrappers. You can buy at Japanese or Chinese supermarkets. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Prawns/shrimp</strong> - add your choice of fresh or frozen prawns, peeled and deveined. Frozen prawns should be defrosted before making it into a mince. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Chives</strong> - add garlic chives which has a unique pungent garlicky fragrant and is ideal for making prawn gyoza. It is also know as Chinese chives or Asian garlic chives. If you cannot get garlic chives, you can simply add spring onions ( green onions ) as a substitute. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Cabbage</strong> - Asian cabbage and sweetheart cabbage are ideal for gyoza fillings which have thin, tender, leaves. You can also use napa cabbage as a substitute.</p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Garlic & ginger</strong> - add freshly grated garlic and ginger, which brings more flavour to the dumplings. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Seasonings</strong> - You will also need a handful of cupboard-friendly seasoning ingredients. Soy sauce, sesame oil, Japanese mirin rice cooking wine, white pepper, and salt to taste. Add a tablespoon of corn starch to bind all the ingredients. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Oil </strong>- fry with neutral flavour oil like canola, sunflower, vegetable oil, etc. </p>

<p class="wp-block-paragraph">To make the dipping sauce, combine soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, and chilli oil in a small bowl. Whisk until sugar dissolved. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Soy sauce</strong> - I usually use Japanese Kikkoman soy sauce when I make Japanese dumplings and dipping sauces. Instead of Japanese soy sauce, you can add your choice of all-purpose soy sauce or light soy sauce. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Vinegar</strong> - rice vinegar is one of the main ingredients to make gyoza sauce. Instead of rice vinegar you can add fresh lemon or lime juice. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Sugar</strong> - I love to add a dash of sugar to adjust the saltiness and sour taste. </p>



<p class="wp-block-paragraph"><strong>Chilli oil </strong>- For a kick of heat, add Japanese chilli oil Layu ( Rayu/ラー油 ) or add your choice of <a href="https://khinskitchen.com/homemade-chilli-oil/">homemade chilli oil</a> or store-bought one. </p>

<ul class="wp-block-list"><li>To wrap the prawn gyoza, place one gyoza pastry in the left palm, and scoop in a tablespoon of fillings in the middle of the wrapper. Dip the index finger in water and wet the edges of the wrapper. Fold the wrapper in half, over the filling. Pinch on one edge, make a pleat, and seal it, as shown in the video and photo instructions.</li><li>Repeat the process with the rest of the wrappers until the filling runs out. ( You can create approximately 30-35 gyoza with this filling. ) Place the folded dumplings in a large tray or plate and cover with wet kitchen towel to prevent them from drying out. </li><li>To pan-fry, heat the flat-bottom non-stick pan/skillet to medium heat. Drizzle a tablespoon of oil and place the gyoza pleat side upward. Fry for 1-2 minutes or until slightly brown. Then add the water, close the lid and cook for 3-4 minutes or until the water dries out. </li><li>Serve immediately with dipping sauce. </li></ul>

<h2 id="frequently-asked-questions"   class="wp-block-heading">Frequently Asked Questions</h2>



<div class="schema-faq wp-block-yoast-faq-block"><div class="schema-faq-section" id="faq-question-1670682483676"><strong class="schema-faq-question">What can I use instead of gyoza wrapper?</strong> <p class="schema-faq-answer">Instead of gyoza paper, you can use Chinese dumpling wrappers, which is also made from plain flour and water. The texture and size and the size of wrappers can be slightly different. </p> </div> <div class="schema-faq-section" id="faq-question-1670682574443"><strong class="schema-faq-question">Can I use cooked prawns?</strong> <p class="schema-faq-answer">Do not recommend cooked prawns/shrimp making gyoza because cooked prawns can be tough and tasteless to use as a dumpling fillings. Suggest to add frozen/fresh prawns or shrimps which is more moist, succulent, and sweet. </p> </div> <div class="schema-faq-section" id="faq-question-1670682585478"><strong class="schema-faq-question">How to make halal prawn gyoza?</strong> <p class="schema-faq-answer">Prawns, vegetables, and all the seasoning ingredients used in this recipe are halal except mirin cooking wine. To make it halal gyoza, you can omit mirin or use halal mirin brands like Wei Lin. </p> </div> </div>

	<div id="recipe-12653-notes" class="wprm-recipe-notes-container wprm-block-text-normal"><h3 class="wprm-recipe-header wprm-recipe-notes-header wprm-block-text-bold wprm-align-left wprm-header-decoration-none" style="">Notes</h3><div class="wprm-recipe-notes"><span style="display: block;"></span><div class="wprm-spacer"></div>
<ul>
<li><strong>Gyoza wrappers</strong> - are made of wheat flour, salt, and water. You can buy it at Japanese or Chinese supermarkets. You can make approximately 30-35 dumplings according to the size of the wrappers you use.  </li>
<li><strong>Prawns/shrimp</strong> - add your choice of fresh or frozen prawns, peeled and deveined. Frozen prawns should be defrosted and pat dry with a paper towel.</li>
<li><strong>Chives</strong> - It is also known as Chinese chives or Asian garlic chives. If you cannot get garlic chives, you can simply add spring onions ( green onions ) as a substitute. </li>
<li><strong>Cabbage</strong> - Asian cabbage and sweetheart cabbage are ideal for gyoza fillings which have thin, tender, leaves. You can also use napa cabbage as a substitute.</li>
<li>Fry with batches and make sure to leave enough space between each gyoza in the pan.</li>
<li>It takes about 3 batches to fry and you will need 6-8 tbsp of water for frying each batch.</li>
<li><strong>Can you freeze it?</strong> Yes, you can freeze it in the freezer for later use. Place the folded uncooked gyoza pieces on the parchment paper in the tray and let it set for about 1 hour to set. Then transfer them to a freezer-safe bag and freeze them. It usually lasts in the fridge for up to 1 month. </li>
<li><strong>Can you reheat fried gyoza? </strong>Gyoza tastes best when freshly fried but if you have any leftovers you can reheat them in the microwave just for a few seconds until warm. </li>
</ul>
